title: Atomic metering for chunked uploads during client-side rate backoff
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Problem: Clients that send large inputs in chunked/streaming requests can trigger client-side rate backoff or retries. The current metering pipeline attributes token credits as fragments arrive, which results in double-charging or undercharging when a client replays/retries portions of an upload during transient rate-limiting. This ticket implements an atomicization strategy so that billing credits for a logical request (which may be delivered as multiple chunks) are finalized only when the request reaches a durable terminal state (success / final abort), while preserving near-real-time quota enforcement and rate-limiter behavior.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Tokens attributable to a logical request are not finalized until a terminal receipt is recorded or a deterministic timeout elapses. 2) Metering does not allow unlimited unfinalized accrual—quota/rate limits enforce provisional reservations preventing abuse. 3) Existing billing reports and downstream pipelines (billing exports, invoices) match pre-change totals for non-replayed traffic. 4) No >1% increase in 99th percentile metering-related latency on the ingest path. 5) Migration/deployment plan validated on staging with synthetic replay scenarios.
implementation_notes: High-level approach: 1) Introduce a lightweight per-session provisional ledger keyed by (customer_id, session_id, logical_request_id). 2) On chunk arrival, compute token delta and increment provisional counter; emit provisional-metering events to Kafka topic metering.provisional. 3) Terminalizer service (shared, horizontally scalable) listens for finalization signals (client marks end, stream EOF, or server-finalized abort) and atomically move provisional balances to committed-metering topic with idempotency token. 4) Quota enforcement uses a hybrid model: a fast in-memory reservation check (Redis) against provisional+committed to decide accept/reject, and a reconciliation job that heals drifts. 5) Provide graceful fallbacks: when terminalizer is unavailable, fall back to legacy immediate-commit path but mark records with migration_flag for later reconciliation.
test_plan: Unit tests for provisional ledger ops and idempotency keys. Integration harness that simulates: intermittent reconnects, duplicate chunk delivery, parallel client retries, and forced terminalizer restarts. E2E load job reproducing 10k concurrent streaming sessions with 10-30 chunks each, with 20% simulated retries. Backfill test: replay last 7 days of production events into staging reconciliation pipeline to verify no billing delta for non-replayed flows. Metrics: token_count_delta, provisional_to_committed_latency, provisional_leak_rate (should be <0.1% per hour), false-positive double-charges (zero expected).
comments: 2026-03-02 - Asha Kapoor: Scoped spike completed. Provisional ledger design looks feasible; Redis hash per session seems easiest but we need to bound memory. Ran small experiment storing 1M provisional keys -> memory growth acceptable with TTL eviction. Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/METER/Atomic+Provisional+Metering

2026-03-04 - Miguel Santos: Implemented provisional counter prototype in ingest-worker branch feat/atomic-metering. Pushed initial events to metering.provisional topic. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1287

2026-03-05 - Priya Menon (PM): Concern about quota UX — if provisional reservations reduce available quota aggressively, customers may observe unexpected rejections. Let's add a conservative reservation factor and a soft-fail path with informative error code. Added as follow-up in acceptance criteria.

2026-03-06 - Design review (informal): Daniel Kim suggested using idempotency token derived from request-id + client-chunk-seq to avoid duplicates. Also suggested emitting structured debug trace for forensic billing investigations. Agreed to add a trace field 'metering.trace_id'.

2026-03-08 - Miguel Santos: Added terminalizer service skeleton and idempotent commit logic. Instrumented provisional_to_committed_latency histogram (Prometheus: metering_provisional_commit_seconds). Deployed to staging with feature flag metering.atomic_provisional=true.

2026-03-09 - QA: Found an edge case where long-lived sessions (over 24h) kept provisional keys alive and inflated provisional reservations. Plan: cap provisional TTL to 6 hours and run background compaction. Added ticket ENG-460124 to handle aggressive-expiry-compaction.
2026-03-11 - Performance note: Ingest path median latency +6ms, p99 +14ms in staging under load test. This meets target (<20ms p99). Will monitor after canary rollout.

2026-03-12 - Security review (preliminary): No customer data persisted beyond existing metering events; provisional ledger only stores counts and ids. Security ok with standard audit logging. Marking security_review_required=false.
notes_for_release: Feature guarded by runtime flag metering.atomic_provisional. Default off for 2 weeks; enable for Canary customers with high-reliability billing then gradual ramp. Post-rollout reconciliation job must run daily for first 30 days and report discrepancies to billing-alerts channel.
rollback_strategy: Flip metering.atomic_provisional=false to revert to immediate-commit path. Reconciliation will need to reconcile any outstanding provisional entries: terminalizer will commit remaining provisional entries within 10 minutes of rollback. If that fails, run bulk-finalize job to convert provisonals to committed with last-seen-state policy.
owner_notes: Priority depends on reducing customer-facing ghost charges seen in incident INC-2026-02. Estimated risk moderate; deliver in two sprints. Coordinate with billing and support teams for communications and post-deploy validation.
